questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is posted where you cannot enter. You may see it on one-way streets or when trying to enter an expressway ramp in the wrong direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve in the road ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions immediately ahead. This sign warns of a curve to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of an upcoming intersection so you can prepare for traffic or plan to turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Upcoming sharp left and right turns.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a winding road ahead. Reduce your speed appropriately.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They inform drivers of traffic laws for that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane will end ahead. Drivers in that lane must merge into another lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right turn on red light permitted with caution.
All traffic must turn right at next intersection.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a diagonal line over a symbol means that action is prohibited. This sign prohibits right turns.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane reduction; the right lane ends soon.
Lane reduction; the left lane ends soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane reduction; the right lane ends soon.
questions.explanation: This sign indicates that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. Turning right here is unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits turns in the direction the arrow points. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community service group is picking up trash along the highway ahead.
Workers are on or very close to the road in the work zone ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or very close to the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: That the right lane ends and traffic should merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the right lane ends and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane is ending. Traffic in the right lane must move to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign alerts you to a steep hill ahead. The hill may be long, steep, or have sharp curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing downward means the lane is open for traffic. You can use this lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop and check for traffic coming from both directions before proceeding.
Give the right-of-way to traffic on the road you wish to enter or cross.
Maintain a steady speed and check for traffic coming from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic on the road you wish to enter or cross.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop if needed. Let other vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians pass before you continue. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve ahead.
Drive no slower than 35 mph around the upcoming curve.
Approach the upcoming curve at a speed of 35 mph or slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the upcoming curve at a speed of 35 mph or slower.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to conditions ahead. A speed advisory sign below it recommends how fast you should go through the upcoming curve. In this case, 35 mph or slower is advised.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange diamond signs mark construction and maintenance work areas. They help guide drivers and pedestrians safely through these zones. Traffic fines may be doubled in these areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic from other lanes may merge into your lane ahead. Be alert and ready for other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is moving in both directions ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings and alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign indicates that a divided highway is starting. Stay to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road ahead.

questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign alerts you that pedestrians may cross the road ahead. You must stop and stay stopped until pedestrians completely cross the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped yellow warning signs alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready to stop for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must and must not do. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: May either continue through the interchange or exit the freeway from your current lane.
May stay in your lane and continue through the interchange.
Must exit the freeway, if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit the freeway, if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your current lane will leave the highway on a ramp. You must either exit the highway or change lanes to stay on the main road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and, if necessary, yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be prepared to stop, and, if necessary, yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Triangular yield signs mean you must slow down at intersections. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians pass before you go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards or special conditions ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.
